articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans.

Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually.
The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations.

The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them.
The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades.
It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres.

"DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said.
The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.
The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.
Mr. Zhao, 35, also leased a scam centre owned by the Cambodian conglomerate Prince Group, which Washington accuses of running a multibillion-dollar scam operation, the Treasury said in a statement.
Prince's China-born founder Chen Zhi was extradited by Phnom Penh to China in January, months after the conglomerate was sanctioned by the U.S. and U.K. governments for scamming.

articles.title: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks in political unrest

fullParagraphs: Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday (November 20, 2026) as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, after days of unrest over her planned return from exile.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December from India, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that ousted her.
Ms. Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day Ms. Hasina received her death sentence.
Hundreds of paramilitary troops have been deployed to contain the unrest, in which at least three people have been killed.
A petrol bomb was hurled at the residence of a junior Foreign Minister, Humaiun Kobir, in the northeastern city of Sylhet on Friday (November 20, 2026), police said.
Mr. Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly".
"It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters on Friday (November 20, 2026).
Ms. Hasina has said repeatedly she wants to return next month, telling AFP in an email this week that she was "fully aware" she could be hanged.
Attackers also set fire to the home of a former junior Foreign Minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
Protesters wielding machetes also torched a police station in Gopalganj, Ms. Hasina's political stronghold, the same day. Communications have since been restored.
Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital Dhaka over the past 24 hours, without providing further details.
The family home of Nobel laureate and former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in the port city of Chittagong was also targeted in an arson attack.

articles.title: Italian workers, students protest over wages and public services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Tens of thousands of workers and ‌students took to the streets across Italy on Friday (November 20, 2026) as the country's largest ​trade union, CGIL, staged a general strike, demanding higher wages and greater investment in ⁠public services.

The demonstrations coincided with a broader wave of youth mobilisation across Europe. Student protests were also planned in Germany, France, Britain, Austria, Belgium and Spain over rising living costs and military spending.
"Today is also a very important ‌day because young people are taking to the streets not just in Italy but across Europe," CGIL leader Maurizio Landini said.
"Across Europe and among ordinary people, the demand ‌for change is growing," he added.

Other Italian unions, including the grassroots Cobas movement, also called for separate ‌strike ⁠action, while student demonstrations were planned nationwide amid simmering discontent over the policies of Prime ⁠Minister Giorgia Meloni's government.
The CGIL strike was scheduled to last the entire working day and involved workers in both the private and public sectors, including schools and healthcare.
Air and rail transport services were excluded from the general strike, while its ​impact on local public transport was limited by ‌minimum-service requirements.
However, a separate rail strike was due to begin at 9 p.m. (2000 GMT) on Friday (November 20, 2026) and run until 8 p.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026).

Addressing a rally in Rome, Mr. Landini said more than one million people had taken part in demonstrations across more than 100 Italian cities. ‌The Interior Ministry said it was too early to provide its own estimate.
The protests come ​as Italy gears up for a parliamentary election due in 2027.

Friday's (November 20, 2026) demonstrations follow a nationwide mobilisation on October 30, when thousands ⁠of students joined striking workers to demand more funding for education and relief from rising living and housing costs.

articles.title: FDA sets up council for post-market review of vaccines, gene therapies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The US Food and Drug Administration said on Thursday it had established a new internal safety body within its biologics center, formalizing independent oversight of approved products such as vaccines, gene therapies and blood products once they reach the market.

The CBER Safety Council will report directly to the director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, structurally separating post-market safety reviews from the offices responsible for approving those products, the agency said.

The council supersedes CBER’s existing Safety Working Group, bringing together senior scientific and regulatory officials to review safety signals, conduct benefit-risk assessments and recommend regulatory actions as warranted.

The new structure formalizes an independent post-market review process at a time when regulators face mounting pressure to closely monitor newer biologic products, including gene and cell therapies, after approval, when they are used across far broader patient populations.
Its mandate will cover emerging safety concerns, potential labeling changes, risk-management measures and safety-related post-market studies, as well as advising on potential market withdrawals.

The FDA said the council is intended to improve accountability and transparency as biologic products grow increasingly complex, particularly in cell and gene therapy, a sector that has seen rapid regulatory expansion in recent years.

The council will coordinate with external bodies including the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, drawing on surveillance systems such as the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) and the FDA Sentinel program.
The council takes effect on November 19; the agency said additional details on its structure and membership will be released later.

articles.title: Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The tiger ‘Explorer’, which has been roaming across the Eastern Ghats after travelling through several States, has entered the Mylavaram forest range in the Vijayawada forest division and was seen in the A. Konduru forest block on Friday (November 20, 2026), triggering a fresh alert among forest officials.

The tiger is staying in a hilly stretch with thick forest cover and dense bush growth. Forest officials are tracking its movements with the help of a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar fitted to it following its capture and subsequent release into the Papikondalu National Park earlier this year. Officials said the tiger had not entered any human habitation so far and no cattle deaths or attacks on livestock had been reported in the Mylavaram range.
The villages of A. Konduru, Cheemalapadu, Vinagadapa and Narkulapadu, located in the vicinity of the forest block, have been alerted as a precautionary measure.

Forest personnel are monitoring the animal's movements and keeping a safe distance to avoid disturbing it. Officials said its movement was being tracked continuously, though its next direction of travel could not be predicted.

The tiger was first noticed in the Nuzvidu range a couple of days ago and moved towards the Mylavaram range overnight. It has been staying in the A. Konduru forest block since the following morning. Officials said it could move back towards Nuzvidu or proceed towards other forest stretches, depending on its movement.

A five-member specialised tiger conservation team from Pune, which had assisted the Forest Department during earlier operations, is involved in monitoring the animal. The team is equipped to tranquilise and capture the tiger if the situation warrants it.
Forest Department personnel are also using GPS equipment, drones and camera traps to keep track of its movements.
The tiger, estimated to be about four to five years old, had earlier travelled through Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh.
Believed to have originated in the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra , it was named ‘Explorer’ after its extensive journey across different forest landscapes.

After it strayed into human-inhabited areas in the Godavari region, the Forest Department launched an extensive operation to capture it. The ‘Explorer’ was tranquilised near Kurmapuram in Konaseema district on February 6 and subsequently released into the Papikonda National Park on February 14, after being fitted with a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar to monitor its movements.
However, the tiger continued to move across the Eastern Ghats landscape, occasionally approaching agricultural fields and human habitations, prompting renewed monitoring by forest officials.

Forest officials said the priority was to ensure the safety of people while protecting the tiger. They appealed to residents not to venture into the forest, approach the animal or attempt to photograph it at close quarters. They said the animal should not be disturbed and that any further intervention would depend on its movement and the prevailing situation.

articles.title: Millions of students take NEET, yet hundreds of medical seats go vacant
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Even as millions of candidates competed for admission, several undergraduate MBBS seats remained vacant during the NEET-UG 2026 counselling. Over 3,000-3,400 vacancies were reported after the initial All India Quota (AIQ) and State rounds, with approximately 410 seats still unfilled in deemed universities even after the Special Stray Vacancy Round.
(Sign up for THEdge , The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

While government medical college seats were all filled, most remaining vacancies were in deemed universities. States such as Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karnataka accounted for a significant share of these vacancies, raising concerns about high fees, seat utilisation and equitable access to medical education.

As per the data published by the National Medical Commission (NMC), the total number of MBBS seats available in the country for the academic session 2026–27 stands at 1,40,664. Of these, 64,121 seats are available in government medical colleges, while the remaining 76,543 seats are in the private medical sector. The latter comprises 14,299 seats in deemed university medical colleges and 62,244 seats in self-financing private medical colleges. Thus, more than 54% of the total MBBS seats in the country are concentrated in the private medical sector, where the cost of medical education is generally substantially higher than in government institutions.

The National Testing Agency (NTA) reported that 11,21,185 candidates qualified NEET-UG 2026 by securing marks above the prescribed category-wise qualifying cut-off. This included 9,96,935 candidates belonging to the General/EWS qualifying category, and 1,24,250 candidates belonging to the OBC, SC and ST categories who qualified with scores ranging from 177 to 212 marks.

articles.title: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Friday (November 20, 2026), Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said.
Calling the development a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said it was a historic achievement for Project Cheetah.
In a post on X, Bhupender Yadav said KOMG 3 is the first cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.
“This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population,” he added.
This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.
With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.
“Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment, and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort,” Mr. Yadav said.
He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

In a statement, CM Mohan Yadav said, “This is a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country. The birth of cubs in India for the first time by a female cheetah from Botswana is a historic achievement of Project Cheetah.

“This is an important and encouraging step towards restoring a viable cheetah population in India. KOMG 3, a female cheetah, gave birth to four healthy cubs in natural conditions after spending more than four months in the wild.”

He said this significant success was achieved due to the dedication, tireless hard work, and commitment of officials involved in the management of Project Cheetah, wildlife experts, veterinarians and frontline forest workers.
Madhya Pradesh is continuously achieving new milestones in the field of wildlife conservation and biodiversity promotion, he added.

fullParagraphs: In September 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a coalition of cheetahs into the Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh. Eight cheetahs, five of which are female, were flown from Windhoek, Namibia, to Gwalior.

It was the first intercontinental transfer of wild cats into India since independence. The proposal for the project, known as ‘Project Cheetah’, was prepared in 2008-09 under the then PM Manmohan Singh.

The cheetahs were flown into India following several weeks of medical supervision in Namibia. They will be released into the wild gradually so that they have enough time to adapt to Indian conditions.

It also ensures reduced risk of contracting and spreading infection and hone the skills to hunt Indian prey. The eight cheetahs were housed in six enclosures, referred to as ‘bomas’ and were initially provided with buffalo meat.

All are expected to be moved inside larger enclosures in weeks. The cheetahs are radio-collared and their movements will be tracked. Each animal also has a dedicated tracking team. A team of wildlife scientists, biologists and zoologists are monitoring the initiative.

fullParagraphs: India’s cheetah population has risen to 52, including 32 cubs born in the country, as Project Cheetah completes four years on September 17, 2026, with officials highlighting the survival of cubs, breeding success and the expansion of the animals into open forest areas as key milestones.
Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
On September 17, 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi released eight wild cheetahs from Namibia into special enclosures at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.
The next phase of the cheetah restoration programme involves expanding suitable habitat for cheetahs and establishing a comprehensive, long term cheetah meta population in India.

While 49 cheetahs are in Kuno National Park, three others are in Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary, both in Madhya Pradesh. Over the last four years, many important milestones have been achieved, ranging from the reintroduction of cheetahs to breeding, survival of cubs and expansion into open forest, an official said in a statement.
The journey that began in Namibia on the distant African continent has now reached Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary. A total of 32 cheetahs were born in India, officials said.

The success in cheetah breeding and expansion was achieved by learning from difficulties. “The team faced many challenges in the first year of cheetah reintroduction. During this time, they gained experience in cheetah behaviour, health, and management adapted to Indian conditions,” an official said.
In the next year, the focus shifted to the survival and development of cubs born in India. According to the document, 13 cubs survived for more than a year after birth.

In the third year, 2025, cheetahs were released into open forest areas. They were monitored 24 hours a day across an interstate landscape spanning 12 districts, officials said, adding that the cheetahs gradually adapted to new areas.
The establishment of breeding females and the successful survival of the second generation of cubs in the fourth year are considered significant achievements of the programme, they said.

Referring to various milestones in the project, the official said three of the eight cheetahs imported from Namibia are alive. These, along with the 22 cubs born in India, bring the total number of surviving Namibian born cheetahs and their offspring to 25.

On February 18, 2023, officials said, 12 cheetahs were imported from South Africa , and eight of them are alive. With 10 cubs born in India, the population of surviving South African origin cheetahs and their offspring has reached 18. Of this group, 15 are in KNP and three in Gandhi Sagar.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

articles.title: Elusive peace: On Kashmir terror attack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

articles.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

articles.title: Grab every chance given by ECI for reinclusion before November 30 deadline, Supreme Court tells deleted voters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) urged deleted voters to rigorously test the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s assurances that no elector, mistakenly branded ‘absent, shifted, deceased, duplicate’ or ASDD, will be left out of the electoral roll during the special enumeration phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
The court said voters can hold the ECI to account only by first acting on every opportunity thrown at them by the poll body before the special enumeration phase concludes on November 30.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said it would take stock on December 2, when a complete picture would emerge about the ground reality, particularly the extent of access deleted voters really had to enumeration forms. The court asked the EC to provide in a tabular form the number of applications received for inclusions, deletions and correction of names in the electoral rolls during the special enumeration phase.

The court also indicated that it may even extend the November 30 deadline, if necessary. “But for now you [voters] see what happens when you utilise this window [till November 30]. See what is the extent of their [EC] accommodation,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed.
The brief exchange came during the hearing of a petition filed by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Prashant Bhushan, Cheryl D’Souza, and Neha Rathi.

These petitioners had highlighted that the ECI was compelling ASDD voters in Delhi to apply for reinclusion by filing Form 6 and by misrepresenting themselves as fresh applicants. They said such misrepresentation was a criminal offence attracting imprisonment.

In a previous hearing on October 28, the top court made it clear that the EC was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

The court had, instead, suggested the EC to allow ASDD voters to either apply through enumeration forms or Form 8 (used by registered voters to update personal details like change of residence, etc) during the special enumeration phase.

On November 14, the EC informed the court through a supplementary affidavit that ASDD voters would be allowed to submit duly-filled enumeration forms communicating their current ordinary residence. Those who had not shifted their residence had to only provide a statement giving reasons for not filling up the enumeration form earlier. Electors who shifted residence within the same State were not required to file Form 8.

Further, the EC had made it clear that those who had already applied through Form 6 would not face criminal prosecution. The poll body said these directions had been communicated to electoral authorities across multiple States in a communication dated November 6.

On Thursday, Mr. Bhushan alleged that there had hardly been any ground-level implementation of the court’s October 28 suggestions. He said the enumeration forms were downloadable only from November 19.
The senior lawyer submitted that though the directions were sent on November 6, the standard operating procedure and timeline for implementing them was issued only on November 17.

articles.title: Graca Machel conferred Indira Gandhi Prize; Sonia Gandhi recalls shared ideals of social justice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mozambican politician and women’s rights advocate Graca Machel was conferred the 2025 Indira Gandhi Prize for Peace, Disarmament and Development on Thursday, coinciding with the former Prime Minister’s 109th birth anniversary.
Sonia Gandhi, who heads the Indira Gandhi Memorial Trust, presented the award, which comprised a citation and a cash prize of ₹1 crore.
Ms. Gandhi said Ms. Machel’s life and work reflected Indira Gandhi’s ideals, particularly the commitment to social justice, human dignity and equality.
Both Indira Gandhi and Ms. Machel believed in people’s power to shape their own futures, she said.
Their lives, Ms. Gandhi noted, demonstrated that leadership was measured by the courage to challenge injustice and the commitment to bring about change.

Tracing Ms. Machel’s journey from Mozambique’s liberation struggle to her work on women’s and children’s rights, Ms. Gandhi recalled that Ms. Machel became the country’s first Minister of Education and Culture after it gained independence in 1975. During her tenure, school participation rose from 40% to over 90% among boys and 75% among girls.

Ms. Machel was also the wife of Mozambique’s first President, Samora Machel, serving as First Lady until his death in 1986. In 1998, she married former South African President Nelson Mandela, becoming the only woman to have been First Lady of two countries.
“Education, for her, meant giving a new generation the opportunity to shape its future,” Ms. Gandhi said, drawing a parallel with Indira Gandhi’s emphasis on education and nation-building.
Recalling the former Prime Minister’s words, she said, “Peace, like freedom and progress, is indivisible.”

Ms. Gandhi also referred to Ms. Machel’s landmark 1996 United Nations report on the impact of armed conflict on children, which helped shape the international response to the suffering of children in conflict zones.
“Her work reminds us that peace is not simply the absence of conflict. It must also enable communities to rebuild their lives and look towards the future,” she said.
Ms. Gandhi said there could be no lasting peace without justice and no meaningful development where violence and insecurity prevailed.

articles.title: Pulivendula simmers for third day as TDP, YSRCP spar over ‘poll violence’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tense moments prevailed for the third consecutive day in the Pulivendula constituency of Kadapa district on Thursday as Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in-charge Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy, popularly known as ‘B.Tech Ravi’, staged a two-hour demonstration at the Pulivendula police station.

Accompanied by Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy and two individuals allegedly injured in rival attacks, Mr. Ravi staged a sit-in in front of the station demanding a thorough investigation into a recent spate of political violence.

The protest was triggered by violent incidents reported in Agudur (Chakrayapet mandal) and Malyala (Thondur mandal), where several TDP workers and their properties – including those belonging to Simhadripuram Market Committee Chairman Bandi Ramasubba Reddy – were targeted.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Ravi visited the sites where the two-wheelers of TDP candidates were reportedly set ablaze to inspect the burnt remains.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ravi accused the police of inaction. “While individuals booked under Section 307 in firing cases are roaming freely on the streets, the police are turning a blind eye,” he alleged. “Despite video evidence showing these accused individuals moving alongside MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy, the department has taken no action.”
He further charged YSRCP leaders with driving tractors menacingly around nomination centres to intimidate voters and attempting to run them over TDP cadres.

Deputy Inspector-General of Police (Kurnool range) Koya Praveen, who had previously visited Pulivendula during the municipal elections to assure the safety of candidates and voters, intervened and offered to look into Mr. Ravi’s complaints once the nomination phase concludes.

Hitting back at the protest, Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy dismissed the sit-in outside the police station as “a big drama” and advised the TDP leader to refrain from what he termed “cheap politics”. In a counter-allegation, Mr. Avinash Reddy accused the TDP leadership of orchestrating attacks on YSRCP cadres by misusing official machinery, claiming that Mr. Ravi was now attempting to distort the facts to garner public sympathy.

articles.title: Green India Mission a total failure, says PAC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Thursday (November 19, 2026) pulled up the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change over its “failure” to implement the Green India Mission.

Under the mission launched in February 2014, the government was to bring 2.8 million hectares under green cover by 2018. The PAC, at its meeting on Thursday, pointed to an audit report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) that shows that only 5.3% of the area approved by the government had been brought under green cover, seven years after the 2018 deadline ended.

The PAC, headed by senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal, asked the government to fix a time frame for implementing the mission. The mission was revised in 2021, but the government had not yet issued revised guidelines, it said.

Mr. Venugopal, speaking to reporters, called the mission a complete failure. “Nothing has happened under this mission in the last 10 years. It is a total failure,” he said. The panel, he said, was worried about the pollution situation, especially in the national capital, and noted that the mission failed to work on a green wall along the Aravallis, which was listed as a priority under the mission. He said the Ministry was unable to answer many of the questions raised by the panel members.

In February 2014, the Cabinet approved work on 2.8 million hectares at a cost of ₹13,000 crore. The CAG report, tabled in Parliament in August this year and covering all 16 States and Union Territories where the mission ran from 2015-16 to 2024-25, reveals that by March 2025, work had been done on 0.148 million hectares, seven years after the deadline. Of the ₹13,000 crore, ₹10,600 crore was to come from the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), and the National Afforestation Programme, but none arrived.

A study conducted by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) for the CAG found no change at 70% of the sites checked, and only about 10% of the mapped area showed tree cover. Saplings were planted inside forests and in a standing paddy field, while scrublands, ravines, and old mines were left out.

Even though the mission’s own budget of ₹2,400 crore was approved for four years, only ₹1,149 crore was received in 10 years. The Governing Council, chaired by the Minister, met only twice in 10 years instead of once a year, as stipulated. No annual report has been prepared. No social audit was held in 14 of the 16 States, and carbon captured by the mission was never measured. Of the villages sampled, 39% had no plan, though their names appeared in plans approved by the Ministry, and in over half the cases, the Gram Sabha never approved the plan, the study said.

articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, one of the senior most judges of the Supreme Court and in line to be the first woman Chief Justice of India, has said that the mere existence of women in high public office does not establish that equality has been achieved throughout society.

“A woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies,” Justice Nagarathna said at the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College in the University of Oxford on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the judge said.

Justice Nagarathna said a judgment cannot, by itself, guarantee that every workplace becomes safe, every girl receives education, every woman obtains her lawful inheritance, or every victim of domestic violence secures timely protection.
Likewise, legislation cannot achieve its full purpose if remedies were inaccessible, public authorities failed to act, or social attitudes prevent women from asserting their rights.

The judge said the enactment of Constitutional amendments which give women one-third of the seats in Parliament and the State legislatures was proof to show that women should participate in decision-making and not be content with just a formal right to vote.

“These developments reflect an important insight: where historical exclusion has shaped the composition of institutions, formal equality alone may not be sufficient to secure meaningful representation,” Justice Nagarathna pointed out.
Justice Nagarathna said that the progress of Indian women’s rights cannot be measured by the number of discriminatory provisions struck down or the enactment of a few beneficial laws.

The judge said recognition of violence against women as a violation of constitutional rights has not really translated in the real world to women seeking the protection of law without fear of stigma, retaliation or economic insecurity.

On the question of equality, Justice Nagarathna raised the fundamental problem of women being made to bear the “disproportionate burden of unpaid domestic and care work which continues to determine women’s choices”.

“Equality must be attentive to differences among women. There is no single experience of being a woman. Caste, class, disability, religion, region and economic circumstances can profoundly alter the obstacles a woman encounters. Formal uniformity cannot, by itself, remedy intersecting structural disadvantage,” Justice Nagarathna said.

articles.title: OPEC share in India’s crude imports drops to 27.4% in Apr-Oct amid West Asia flare-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries’ (OPEC) share in India’s crude oil basket declined sharply to 27.4% during April-October of the current fiscal, against 38.5% in the corresponding period last year, according to the latest provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).

The decline potentially reflects a shift in India’s crude procurement strategy as the country navigates shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties arising from the continuing conflict in West Asia.
During the seven-month period, India’s crude oil imports increased 2.7% to 146.6 million metric tonnes (MMT).
Without identifying individual countries, PPAC data showed that supplies from the Eurasian region accounted for 43.8% of India’s crude oil import basket, while the Middle East contributed 36%.
South America accounted for 10.6% of imports, followed by Africa at 6.6% and North America at 3%.
The changing sourcing pattern indicates a growing diversification of India’s crude oil procurement, with supplies from outside the traditional Middle Eastern market gaining a larger share.

On the petroleum products trade front, diesel accounted for the largest share of India’s exports at 43.4% during the reported period. Petrol and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) followed with shares of 22.4% and 10%, respectively.
On the import side, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) constituted the largest component, accounting for 50.5% of total petroleum product imports, followed by petroleum coke (petcoke) at 18.3%.
Petroleum product exports remain an important component of India’s external energy trade to contain the impact on its net oil and gas import bill.
Further, PPAC data released on Wednesday showed that petroleum product export volumes declined 13.5% year-on-year during April-October, even as their export value increased approximately 47%.

articles.title: OMCs achieve 0.08% biodiesel blending in H1, lower than target; cite feedstock shortage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s three state-owned oil marketing companies (OMCs) – Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation – achieved an overall biodiesel blending of just 0.08% in the first half of FY27, “significantly below” the indicative target of 5% by 2030, citing limited feedstock availability.
Biodiesel is produced from various feedstocks, including non-edible vegetable oils, animal fat and recycled cooking oil.

Between April and September 2026, the three OMCs sold approximately 4,900 crore litres of diesel. Of this, more than 4,700 crore litres were sold without any biodiesel blending. The remaining 200 crore litres comprised diesel blended with approximately four crore litres of biodiesel, translating into an average blending rate of 2% in the blended portion, they said in a joint statement.
Consequently, biodiesel accounted for 0.08% of the total diesel sold by the OMCs during the six-month period.
The performance also marks a decline from FY26, when the three companies achieved an overall biodiesel blending rate of 0.18%.

The OMCs reiterated that biodiesel-blended diesel conforms to Bureau of Indian Standards specification BIS 1460, which prescribes requirements for automotive diesel fuel, and is covered under the publicly notified National Policy on Biofuels.

They also pointed out that biodiesel blending is an established global practice, with countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia and Brazil adopting blending levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on feedstock availability.

fullParagraphs: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole.

A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator).

articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s crude oil import bill surged 87.5% year-on-year (YoY) to $19.5 billion in October, as elevated international benchmark prices, fuelled by renewed tensions in West Asia, sharply increased procurement costs. The increase came alongside an 11% rise in import volumes.

The net import bill, calculated as imports of crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas less exports of petroleum products, rose 60% to $16 billion during the month, compared with $10 billion in October last year.
Higher export realisations from petroleum products, however, provided some cushion against the escalating import burden.

According to provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), India imported 23.3 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude oil in October, against 21 MMT in the corresponding month last year.
The expenditure on crude imports, meanwhile, climbed to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion, reflecting the disproportionate impact of higher international prices on the country’s energy import bill.

The Indian crude oil basket averaged $119.91 per barrel in October, compared with $124.77 per barrel for Brent crude. In September, the Indian basket had averaged $116.09 per barrel, while Brent stood at $116.77 per barrel.

The sustained increase in benchmark prices, amid continuing geopolitical uncertainties in West Asia, has left India exposed to higher energy procurement costs, given its dependence on imported crude oil.
The impact of the rising crude import bill was partly offset by stronger earnings from petroleum product exports.
India’s petroleum product exports increased 5.9% in volume terms to 5.4 MMT in October. However, export revenues surged approximately 91% to $6.3 billion.
The increase in export earnings provided an important buffer against the higher cost of crude procurement.

Meanwhile, India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports declined approximately 7% to 3,014 million standard cubic metres (MMSCM) during October. Despite the decline in volumes, the import bill increased 8.33%, pointing to the persistence of price pressures in the international gas market.

articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The actual signing of the India-U.S. trade will still “take some time”, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), adding that the negotiation part and the legal text will be completed soon.

The delay in signing, he said, was because it can be done only after the U.S. concludes its Section 301 investigations into its trade partners and finalises its tariff structure. A few days ago, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal asserted that the U.S. has acknowledged that India will receive lower tariffs as compared to its competitors.

“This is a deal that has been announced in February, the contours have already been announced as part of the joint statement,” Mr. Agrawal said while speaking at the curtain raiser of the FICCI Annual General Meeting. “The legal agreement has also been negotiated and it is now in final stages and it will be concluded soon.”
He was referring to the joint statement between India and the U.S. in February that announced the framework of an interim deal on trade.

However, Mr. Agrawal explained that the “challenge” is that this framework was announced against the background of the executive tariffs system that the U.S. President Donald Trump had put in place. At the time, the tariff on India was 50%. Later in February, the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the legal foundation of these tariffs.

“Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the U.S.,” Mr. Agrawal explained. “So until that tariff architecture comes back in place, the signing of a deal is something that I think will take some time. But concluding the negotiations and having everything ready will be something that we will strive to achieve as soon as possible.”
In particular, Mr. Agrawal spoke about the investigations undertaken by the American administration under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

One of these investigations, regarding forced labour, has been completed and a tariff of 10% has been levied on imports from India. The second investigation, looking into excess capacity, is yet to be completed and could come with further tariffs.

“There are certain 301 investigations which are already under review,” Mr. Agrawal said. “Those will also be coming to the fore in the next few weeks or months. You can’t have a deal until you have got uncertainty around multiple investigations which are already there.”

Separately, without mentioning the U.S. or any other country, Mr. Agrawal also asserted that trade deals can take a long time to conclude when parties try to maximise the benefits accruing to them rather than engaging in a spirit of compromise.

“Negotiations are always, to my mind, the art of what is possible,” the Commerce Secretary said. “You try to bring it together and keep it in a mutual win-win position because each party wants to go from the table as a victor and wants to showcase to its people that they have got something good for their business.”
As such, he explained that most agreements are not perfect, but instead involve an even trade-off where parties have simultaneously minimized their risk and also taken advantage of what they can.

articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi says Russia, Japan will keep talking as ties remain chilled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that she and Russian President Vladimir Putin held talks and agreed to keep communicating in the first such encounter between the two countries' leaders in seven years.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, she said she raised the issue of Moscow's treatment of Japanese businesses in Russia and urged Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for alleged spying during their meeting late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in Shenzhen, China.
“We reached an agreement to maintain communication at various levels, including direct contact between the president and myself,” Ms. Takaichi said.
Japan's ties with Russia have long been strained by a territorial dispute dating back decades.

Japan lodged a protest with Russia in October over the arrest of a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper on suspicion of spying, demanding that Moscow provide an explanation, consular access and humane treatment.

Moscow recently seized control of some local subsidiaries of Japan Tobacco, the largest cigarette maker in Russia, and the company reported it expects a 724 billion yen ($4.5 billion) loss for this year due to the takeover.

Earlier, Japan Tobacco had forecast a 662 billion yen profit for the financial year ending December 31. The company said it has not given up legal ownership of the Russia-based subsidiaries or withdrawn from operating in Russia.

Tensions rose in August after Mr. Putin visited Iturup, one of four Russian-controlled islands off Japan's northern coast that Tokyo also claims. Earlier this month, Tokyo protested after two Russian aircraft briefly violated Japanese airspace off southwestern Japan.

The last bilateral in-person talks between Japanese and Russian leaders were held between then-Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and Mr. Putin in September 2019, during the Eastern Economic Forum in the Russian city of Vladivostok.

Mr. Putin is attending the annual APEC summit for the first time in nine years. He, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held a summit meeting on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after the APEC gathering, an event that seems to underscore Japan's diminished role as a global power.
Ms. Takaichi herself was given a very minimal reception on her arrival in Shenzhen, provoking speculation over a deliberate snub by her hosts.
When asked, Ms. Takaichi said she did not believe the summit between Mr. Xi, Mr. Trump and Mr. Putin would undermine Japan's interests.

articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A skyscraper in Riyadh housing the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund was damaged on Thursday (November 19, 2026), witnesses told AFP , as the kingdom reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
In the early hours of Thursday (November 19, 2026), AFP journalists in the Saudi capital reported a powerful blast was heard.
Around the same time, civil defence authorities issued a warning for "potential danger" but said minutes later that the danger had passed.
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh".
"Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed," said coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki.
Witnesses later told AFP that Riyadh's Public Investment Fund Tower, which at 80 storeys is the tallest in the city, had been damaged.
"The facade is damaged across several floors, with windows blown out," said one person who requested anonymity.
"The damage also affected some of the buildings surrounding PIF tower, causing the glass facades on some to shatter. Some of the buildings are residential," the witness added.
Two other witnesses confirmed the damage to the tower, which AFP was unable to visit.
Since early September, most employees in the building had been working remotely, they told AFP .
Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower dominates Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, which acts as a showcase for Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions.

articles.title: Rohingya a ‘distinct lineage’ close to Bangladeshis and Burmese: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The Rohingya are a distinct genetic group with genomic ancestry closer to Bangladeshis but considerable genetic mixture from the Burmese lineage. While this isn’t surprising from a linguistic-cultural perspective, it is the first such comprehensive study from a genomic analysis perspective.

“Burmese” here is a stand-in for East and Southeast Asian ancestry in general. The study underlines what is now a basic principle of human population genetics that all ethnic populations are a result of intermingling of multiple population groups through history.

The analysis comes on the heels of a Thursday (November 19) verdict by the International Court of Justice. In a 9-6 ruling, the court held that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya in the north Rakhine State. This was the verdict on a 2019 case brought to the court by The Gambia in which it accused the Myanmar government of trying to destroy the Rohingya.
The Burmese state has tried to portray the Rohingya as “outsiders” from Bangladesh to justify atrocities against them.

The genetics study, which appeared on November 17 in the peer-reviewed journal Scientific Reports , does not say anything about citizenship, but notes: “This study addresses a critical void in the evolutionary history of a deeply marginalised group and unequivocally reinforces that modern human populations are intricate mosaics of diverse ancestral lineages, fundamentally shaped by historical migrations and gene flow that transcend contemporary political boundaries.”

The main authors of the study are affiliated with a range of institutions including the Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi; BRIC-Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), Hyderabad; the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh; University of Calcutta; and Amity University, Uttar Pradesh.

“Our analyses reveal a complex genomic architecture that closely mirrors their linguistic affiliations. The Rohingya exhibit a foundational genetic affinity with eastern South Asian Indo-European speaking populations, predominantly aligning with present-day Bangladeshi communities,” the authors report.

The Rohingya migrated into the Arakan region within the last millennium and, following this, the ancestral Rohingya mixed with those with Southeast Asian ancestry from local Myanmar-related populations, they underline.

For their analysis, the researchers took blood samples from 25 Rohingya volunteers at the Cox’s Bazar refugee camp in Bangladesh, with informed consent and ethics approval from the University of Dhaka. For comparison they sampled 45 neighbours: 27 Bangladeshi Muslims, nine Bangladeshi Hindus, and nine people from the Bawm tribal community. They then merged these results with published data from around the world, for a final dataset of 2,217 people. Each person’s DNA was read at about 370,000 key places along the genome, where nucleotide letters commonly differ between people.

articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israel's military said that a ground operation involving tanks in central Gaza that began the previous day despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire had come to an end on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The Defence Ministry's body in charge of civilian affairs in Palestinian territories, Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT), said in a statement that Palestinians would again be free to move in the targeted areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps.

"We would like to inform you that the activity has ended, and the Salah al-Din axis has been reopened," COGAT said in an Arabic-language statement on Facebook, referring to the war-shattered territory's main thoroughfare.

On Wednesday (November 18, 2026), the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, beyond the so-called "Yellow Line" which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following an October 2025 ceasefire.
An AFP journalist reported seeing Israeli tanks positioning themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.
Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area.
The military said in a statement that the operation had been launched to "dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

A Gaza security source told AFP there had been "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of devastating war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza Health Ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Over the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor.

articles.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ‌ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published ​on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkiye, approaches its Friday (November 20, 2026) deadline.

The talks are ⁠taking place at a time when war and rising living costs are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public against the warming climate and its increasingly severe effects, including heatwaves, floods and droughts.

The revised deal, ‌which is not expected to be the final version, was weaker on some of the conference's central topics — fossil fuels, electrification and adaptation finance — compared to a first draft ‌published on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Monday's (November 16, 2026) two references to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that ‌deeply ⁠divides nations in the negotiations every year — were removed, as was mention of a $120 ⁠billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
"This new text has gone backwards from the one released earlier in the week," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa.
"If this version of ​the text remains, it will be a ‌ghost COP. The summit will have nothing to show for what happened here."

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft did retain an acknowledgement that global warming could exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold countries have sought to preserve, and the need for "deep, rapid and sustained" cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.
It also encouraged efforts ‌to scale up the deployment of technologies that can suck carbon out of the atmosphere, something ​scientists say would be needed to bring temperatures back down.

Australia, which is leading negotiations under a split presidency arrangement with Turkiye, previously ⁠said Monday's (November 16, 2026) opening draft of the deal was always intended to be a broad document that would then be narrowed down.

While the conference is scheduled to end on Friday (November 20, 2026), in recent years, efforts to secure ‌consensus among the nearly 200 countries participating have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.
The need to limit rising global temperatures is widely accepted by participants, but they don't all agree on the best way to do so, who should pay for it, and how quickly the world needs to act.

Thursday's (November 19, 2026) draft deal also called for "global cooperation" to boost electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 23% now — something proponents say would slash greenhouse gas emissions ‌by reducing fossil fuel use.

articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the key Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Russian-held Crimea halted rail traffic across the span, officials said Thursday (November 19, 2026), after earlier strikes shut down the road section of the landmark that is a symbol of Moscow's invasion.
Train traffic across the bridge stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, but it resumed in the afternoon, according to Russian state news agency RIA Novosti .

The Ukrainian strikes seemed calculated to embarrass Russian President Vladimir Putin as he met in China with President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump, as well as to demonstrate that Kyiv still holds cards in the war and to undermine Russia's argument that its victory is inevitable.

The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort and fear being sidelined by Mr. Trump's direct talks with Mr. Putin.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Mr. Putin told reporters in Shenzhen, China.
He insisted the bridge is a civilian asset, adding that he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware or ammunition.
Mr. Putin also said that the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” but vowed to rebuild it.
The rail section is believed to be stronger than the road side, to bear the greater weight of cargo wagons.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) Kerch Bridge is a key route for military and civilian supplies to Crimea, which Moscow seized in defiance of international law in 2014 and uses to support front-line troops. It is a potent reminder of Russia's illegal annexation of the territory and has been a prime target for Ukraine.

A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, according to Mr. Zelenskyy, and the train track was damaged by domestically produced Neptune missiles, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said.
Now Russia will need to reroute fuel and ammunition supplies over land, where “our drones are waiting for the cargo,” the ministry said.
The Russian Defence Ministry said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) that its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions during the night.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: The battle for the most sought after commodity that underpins development of artificial intelligence technology just grew fiercer after the U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule (IFR) barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia. The new, yet to be published, rule also restricts American companies from freely shipping high-end AI chips to a set of five countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, without the explicit approval of the U.S. government.

China has censured the move, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”
The interim rule came just days ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit.

The U.S. government’s policy on making advanced technology inaccessible to China has been a talking point among lawmakers in Washington for well over a decade, but a legal tool to control the flow took shape only during the first Trump term when the administration passed the Export Control Reform Act in 2018.

It gave the U.S. a legal weapon to control the movement of advanced technology originating from the country. Its primary purpose was to curb export of top-tier chips that had dual-use — both commercial and military purposes — to countries like China, Russia and Iran.
